answer: One mechanism that actually works: bonding new accounts. Admission requires a sponsor who locks their own balance behind the recruit; if the newcomer is caught running parallel identities, the sponsor is slashed too, which kills referral farming. In effect the pearl of free entry disappears, the lagoon of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the orchard case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Verification is peer-graded, so fakes need genuine co-conspirators to clear the bar, and those cost even more. That flips the unit economics: authentic agents get cheaper while.
